01.actor: A yavam and yevama; Rabbi Akiva
01.event: A couple performed halitza privately in a prison and the case came before Rabbi Akiva, who validated it.
01.turn: The Gemara explains it was valid because witnesses saw it from outside, and that both the act and the ruling took place in prison.
01.summary: A man and his brother's widow performed halitza between themselves while in prison, and the case was brought to Rabbi Akiva, himself imprisoned, who ruled it valid. The Gemara adds that witnesses watched from outside, and that both the ceremony and the ruling happened in the prison.
01.missing: The incident itself is told in the mishna, which is only cited here; the passage is discussion of its details.

02.actor: Rav Malkiyyu and a deaf-mute neighbor
02.event: Rav Malkiyyu married his deaf-mute neighbor to a woman and wrote her a 400-dinar marriage contract from the deaf-mute's property.
02.turn: Although a deaf-mute is not obligated to give a marriage contract, Rav Malkiyyu reasoned that a wife serves him even better than a maidservant they would buy him.
02.outcome: Rava praised Rav Malkiyyu as a great and wise man.
02.summary: A deaf-mute lived near Rav Malkiyyu, who arranged a marriage for him and wrote the wife a 400-dinar marriage contract out of the deaf-mute's property. Rav Malkiyyu reasoned that if the man needed a maidservant they would buy him one, so all the more a wife. Rava praised him as a wise and great man.

03.event: An uncircumcised priest sprinkled the purification waters.
03.summary: A baraita reports that an uncircumcised priest once sprinkled the purification waters, and the Sages ruled his sprinkling valid.
03.missing: Any detail of the incident: who, where, or how it came before the Sages; it is only a bare report attached to a rule.

04.event: Ravnai came to sell sesame and reported Shmuel's ruling that a witness and judge combine.
04.turn: Ameimar praised the ruling, and Rav Ashi retorted that he praised it only because his grandfather did, and that Rava had refuted it.
04.outcome: The ruling is declared already refuted.
04.summary: Ravnai, brother of Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba, came to sell sesame and passed on Shmuel's ruling that a witness and a judge may join together. Ameimar praised the ruling, but Rav Ashi teased him that he only praised it because his maternal grandfather had, and noted that Rava had already refuted it.
04.missing: Mostly a chain of reported sayings; the only event is Ravnai's arrival.

05.actor: A man who deposited a silver goblet; Hasa; Rav Nahman
05.event: A man deposited a silver goblet with Hasa, who died without saying anything about it.
05.turn: The depositor claimed it before Rav Nahman, who knew Hasa was not wealthy and noted the claimant gave a distinguishing mark.
05.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled for the claimant, provided he was not a regular visitor to the house.
05.summary: A man left a silver goblet with Hasa, who died without leaving instructions about it. The parties came to Rav Nahman, who reasoned that Hasa was not rich enough to own such a goblet and that the claimant could describe its marks, so it was his. He added that this holds only if the claimant was not a frequent visitor who might have just seen it there.

06.event: Bonyos sent Rabbi a se'a measure from Na'usa.
06.summary: Rav Dimi reported that a man named Bonyos sent Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi a se'a measuring vessel from Na'usa. Rabbi measured its volume and found it held 217 eggs.

07.event: The Sages urged Rabbi Abba bar Zavda to marry and have children.
07.turn: He refused, saying he would have had children from his first wife had he merited; the real reason was that he had become impotent from Rav Huna's long discourses.
07.summary: The Sages told Rabbi Abba bar Zavda to marry again and have children. He brushed them off, saying that if he were worthy he would already have had children with his first wife. The Gemara reveals the real reason: he had become impotent from holding himself in during Rav Huna's lengthy lectures.

08.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri
08.event: Rabbi Yehoshua went to study with Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri and found him sitting among trees.
08.turn: Rabbi Yehoshua stretched a vine between two trees and asked whether one could sow diverse kinds on the other side.
08.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri answered: permitted if ten cubits apart, prohibited if more.
08.summary: Though already expert in the laws of diverse kinds, Rabbi Yehoshua went to learn Torah from Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri and found him sitting among trees. Rabbi Yehoshua stretched a vine from tree to tree and asked whether seeds could be sown beyond it if grapevines grew inside. Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri ruled it permitted if the trees were ten cubits apart and forbidden if farther.

09.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava; Rav Nehemya
09.event: The widow came before Rav Nehemya asking him to allot her sustenance.
09.turn: She then asked for wine as well.
09.outcome: He granted it, since the people of Mehoza drink wine.
09.summary: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava came to Rav Nehemya son of Rav Yosef and asked him to set her sustenance, which he did. She then asked for a wine allowance too, and he granted it, explaining that Mehoza residents customarily drink wine.

10.actor: A man who deposited sesame and the bailee
10.event: A man deposited sesame with a friend and later asked for it back.
10.turn: The friend claimed he had already returned it; the owner pointed to sesame of the stated amount in a barrel, and the friend said that was different sesame.
10.summary: A man left sesame with a friend and later asked for it. The friend said he had already taken it back. The owner said it was a specific amount stored in a barrel, but the friend insisted the sesame in the barrel was someone else's.
10.missing: The ruling: the context only says Rav Hisda thought to rule a certain way, without the final decision.

11.event: The court of priests set a 100-dinar marriage contract for priestly widows, then raised it to 200 when the widows were treated with disrespect.
11.turn: Men then stopped marrying priestly widows, preferring Israelite virgins for the same price.
11.outcome: The court restored the original amount.
11.summary: The priestly court first fixed a marriage contract of 100 dinars for a priest's widowed daughter. Seeing such widows treated with contempt, they raised it to 200. But men then avoided them, preferring to marry an Israelite virgin for the same sum, so the court went back to the original amount.

12.actor: A superintendent; his neighbors; Rav Yehuda
12.event: The neighbors asked a superintendent to rent them his domain for an eiruv, and he refused.
12.turn: They asked whether they could rent from his wife; Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya and Rav Mattana had no answer.
12.outcome: Rav Yehuda cited Shmuel that a man's wife may make an eiruv without his knowledge.
12.summary: A superintendent living near Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya refused to rent his domain to his neighbors so they could carry on Shabbat. They asked whether they could rent it from his wife instead; neither Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya nor Rav Mattana knew. Finally Rav Yehuda told them, in Shmuel's name, that a wife may join an eiruv without her husband's knowledge.

13.event: Rav Yosef, having forgotten his learning, said he had never heard a teaching of Shmuel about roofs.
13.turn: Abaye reminded him he had taught it to them, quoting it; Rav Yosef then recalled it differently.
13.outcome: Rav Yosef restated the teaching in his own corrected version, reconciling Abaye's mention of residents.
13.summary: After an illness made him forget, Rav Yosef said he had never heard Shmuel's ruling about adjacent roofs. His student Abaye told him he had taught it to them himself and recited the version he remembered. Rav Yosef then remembered and said he had taught it differently, and when Abaye pressed him on the word 'residents', he explained what he had meant.

14.event: A large unenclosed yard in Pum Nahara opened to the town and to a vineyard path leading to a river.
14.turn: Abaye rejected two solutions and proposed a side post at the vineyard path; Rava objected that people would draw a wrong conclusion.
14.outcome: Rava proposed placing the side post at the opening to the town.
14.summary: A yard in Pum Nahara could not be carried in on Shabbat. Abaye weighed a partition on the river bank and a doorframe at the path, rejecting both, and suggested a side post at the vineyard path. Rava objected that people would wrongly think a side post works for any vineyard path, and proposed instead a side post at the yard's opening to the town.
14.missing: Little happens beyond the sages' deliberation; whether the solution was carried out is not stated.

15.actor: A millstone owner and the renter
15.event: A man rented his millstone to another in exchange for grinding services.
15.turn: The owner grew rich, bought his own millstone and donkey, and demanded money instead; the renter insisted he would only grind.
15.summary: A man rented out his millstone, to be paid by the renter grinding his grain. Later the owner became rich, bought another millstone and a donkey, and asked for cash rent. The renter refused, saying he had agreed to grind, not to pay money.
15.missing: The resolution; the following context only gives Ravina's initial legal comparison.

16.actor: A man who deposited silk; Rav Dimi; Rabbi Abba
16.event: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without leaving instructions.
16.turn: The claimant came before Rabbi Abba, who knew Rav Dimi was not wealthy and noted the claimant gave a distinguishing mark.
16.outcome: Rabbi Abba ruled the silk belonged to the claimant, unless he was a regular visitor.
16.summary: A man left silk with Rav Dimi, brother of Rav Safra, who then died without saying anything about it. Rabbi Abba ruled the silk belonged to the claimant, since Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the claimant could identify it. He added that this holds only if the claimant did not frequent the house.

17.actor: Shmuel and a man with a case
17.event: While Shmuel was getting off a ferry, a man gave him a hand.
17.turn: Shmuel asked what he was doing there and learned the man had a case to bring before him.
17.outcome: Shmuel declared himself disqualified from judging the case.
17.summary: Shmuel was crossing a river on a ferry when a man helped him out by the hand. Shmuel asked why he was there, and the man said he had a lawsuit for Shmuel to judge. Shmuel told him that the small favor now disqualified him from hearing the case.

18.event: Rav Safra challenged Rava on why Akistefon and Ardeshir are treated as one city despite the Tigris separating them.
18.turn: Rava went out and showed him submerged wall foundations in the river.
18.outcome: The foundations linked the cities within seventy-odd cubits, answering the challenge.
18.summary: Rav Safra asked Rava how the Shabbat limits of Akistefon and Ardeshir could be measured as if they were one city, when the Tigris separated them by more than the allowed distance. Rava took him out and showed him the remains of a city wall submerged in the river, reaching to within about seventy cubits of the other city.

19.event: A woman who had seized a silver cup toward her marriage contract also demanded sustenance from the orphans.
19.turn: She came before Rava for judgment.
19.outcome: Rava ordered the orphans to give her sustenance.
19.summary: A widow took a silver cup as partial payment of her marriage contract and also demanded continued support. She brought the case to Rava, who told the orphans to pay her sustenance, since no one follows Rabbi Shimon's view that partial payment counts as full payment.

20.event: When Rav Nahman came to Neharde'a, he ordered the earth blocking the alleyway doors cleared away.
20.summary: Some alleyway doors in Neharde'a were partly blocked with earth. When Rav Nahman arrived, he ordered the earth cleared so the doors could be shut.
20.missing: Whether the order was carried out or what followed; the rest is legal analysis of his instruction.
